title: Exploring the Challenges and Opportunities in using Compact Direct Electron Detectors for Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD)
content: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) is now a commonly used technique in the scanning electron microscope (SEM). Through analyzing Kikuchi diffraction patterns, which are direct projection of the crystal lattice planes, this technique is able to characterize the microstructure of crystalline materials, including the presence of grains and grain boundaries, crystalline phase analysis, evidence of plastic strain including the analysis of geometrically necessary dislocations (GND), and even variations in elastic strain. The breadth of techniques available has been driven largely by modern software algorithms and the access to reliable hardware for detection, typically through indirect detection using CCD or CMOS based cameras attached to a scintillator screen.
